short: One term of undeclared naval war and the Alien and Sedition Acts.
full:
Adams won the 1796 election by three electoral votes and governed with his defeated rival Thomas Jefferson as vice president, the last time the two offices were filled by opponents. French seizures of American shipping pushed him into the Quasi-War, fought at sea from 1798 to 1800 without any declaration.

He resisted pressure from his own Federalists for full war and sent a peace mission that produced the Convention of 1800. The domestic cost was heavy: the Alien and Sedition Acts of 1798 criminalised criticism of the government, jailed newspaper editors, and provoked the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions asserting a state right to judge federal law. Adams moved into the unfinished White House in November 1800 as its first occupant, lost the election weeks later, and left the capital before Jefferson's inauguration. The transfer of power to an opposing party was the first of its kind.
